Brief Hospital Course:
ACUTE ISSUES:
==========================
#  Diarrhea: On admission patient reported copious amounts of 
brown watery diarrhea over the 2 days prior to admission. She 
states that she had 10 episodes of diarrhea in the ED, but 
patient's sister who was with her at the time denies this.  
Stool was guaiac negative. No fevers or grossly bloody stools to 
suggest infectious colitis, although patient had been treated 
with antibiotics during recent hospitalization. Stool C. diff 
toxin assay was negative. Stool culture and campylobacter assay 
were pending at the time of diagnosis. She was continued on a 
regular diet without nausea, vomiting, or further diarrhea on 
the day of discharge. 

 
#  Cirrhosis, history of portal HTN, ascites, and HE: 
Well compensated Childs B EtOH cirrhosis. During this admission 
she had no signs or symptoms of hepatic encephalopathy. No signs 
of bleeding, with stable hemoglobin and INR at baseline 1.4-1.5. 
 She complained of abdominal and back pain, but had no fever or 
exam findings of SBP.  Only trace ascites by imaging, and 
paracentesis was not performed. Home doses of spironolactone and 
furosemide were held during admission to avoid ___ given concern 
for diarrhea and while other infectious work-up was pending. 
These were restarted upon discharge.  WBC 12.8 on admission, 
decreased to 8.4 on day of discharge.   She was continued on 
lactulose and rifaximin for HE prophylaxis. 

#Abdominal pain: Patient presented with acute worsening of 
chronic lower abdominal pain, likely related to abdominal 
distention in setting of chronic liver disease with 
hepatomegaly. No signs of gallbladder disease, hepatic vascular 
pathology/obstruction on RUQ ultrasound. Exam was notable for 
tensely distended abdomen but no tenderness, guarding, or 
rebound was noted on exam.  Suspect that lower abdominal pain 
was related to diarrhea. SBP was considered unlikely given 
relatively benign abdominal exam and small volume of ascites 
fluid. She did not receive antibiotics this admission. Urine 
culture was positive for coagulase negative staph, however her 
urinalysis was negative and she did not complain of dysuria or 
suprapubic pain. She received a dose of oxycodone 2.5mg PO for 
pain control.
